decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 5% to 5.25%. The vote was 11-0.

changes.quote: Economic activity expanded at a modest pace in the first quarter.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains have picked up in recent months and are running at a robust pace; the unemployment rate has remained low.”

changes.quote: Recent indicators point to modest growth in spending and production.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Tighter credit conditions for households and businesses are likely to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Recent developments are likely to result in tighter credit conditions for households and businesses and to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation.”

changes.quote: The extent of these effects remains uncertain.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The extent of these effects is uncertain.”

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 5 to 5-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.”

tone_quotes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 5 to 5-1/4 percent.

In determining the extent to which additional policy firming may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 19.07% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.38% and moved -6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.39% would fall by about $11.76 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 3.5%, and employers added an average of 264k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.9% over the past year (March 2023); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 4.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -8 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.7%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.41% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 29%, cut 1%, hike 70%.
